neutral_facts.value: The accused was charged with offences punishable under Sections 302 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code. To prove he was a juvenile at the time of the incident, he submitted a school leaving certificate issued by the Principal of a school. The certificate indicated his date of birth as 10.05.1991. The accused provided testimony from the Head Mistress of the school, who confirmed the authenticity of the certificate. The respondent contested the certificate, leading to an enquiry by the Juvenile Justice Board. The Board sought the opinion of a Medical Board, which opined the accused was approximately 20 years old at the time of the incident. The Sessions Judge set aside the JJ Board's order, directing the case back to the JJ Board for trial. The High Court restored the JJ Board's order, but the Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, reinstating the Sessions Judge's order. The Supreme Court concluded that the school leaving certificate was valid and that the accused was a juvenile at the time of the incident, thus the case should be tried by the JJ Board.
